## Notice of the 45" Annual General Meeting
Notice is hereby given that the 45th Annual General Meeting (AGM) of the members of Infosys Limited ("the Company") will be held on Tuesday, June 23,2026,at 4.00 p.m. IST through video conference other audio-visual means ("VC") to transact the following business:
## Ordinary business
## Item no: 1 Adoption of financial statements
To consider and adopt the audited financial statements (including the consolidated financial statements) of the Company for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 and the reports of the Board of Directors ("the Board") and auditors thereon:
## Item no: 2 Declaration of dividend
To declare a final dividend of <25/- per equity share for the financial year ended March 31,2026.
## Item no. 3 Appointment of Nandan M: Nilekani as a director; liable to retire by rotation
To appoint a director in place of Nandan M. Nilekani (DIN: 00041245), who retires by rotation and being eligible, seeks reappointment:
Explanation: Based on the terms of appointment; executive directors, and the non-executive and non-independent chairman are subject to retirement by rotation: Nandan M Nilekani, who was initially appointed on August 24,2017 and last appointed on June 26,2024,and whose office is liable to retire at the ensuing AGM, being eligible; seeks reappointment: Based on his performance evaluation and the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, the Board recommends his reappointment:
To consider and ifthought fit; to pass the following resolution as an ordinary resolution:
RESOLVED THAT pursuant to the provisions of Section 152 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act; 2013,the approval of members of the Company, be and is hereby accorded to reappoint Nandan M. Nilekani (DIN: 00041245) as a director who is liable to retire by rotation.

Approval of the proposed amendment to the Infosys Expanded Stock Ownership Program 2019 (such amended plan is hereinafter referred as the "Amended 2019 Plan") and grant of stock incentives to the eligible employees of the Company and its subsidiaries under the Amended 2019 Plan:
The Company has been a pioneer in India by rewarding its employees through stock ownership programs starting in 1994. This philosophy has created a culture of aligning employee and shareholder interests The 2015 Incentive Compensation Plan ("2015 Plan") was approved by shareholders pursuant to the postal ballot dated March 31,2016,and stock incentives continue to be granted to the eligible employees of the Company thereunder The vesting criteria for stock incentives under the 2015 Plan are largely time-based:
The existing plan was approved by shareholders pursuant to the Annual General Meeting held on June 22, 2019. The shareholders had approved the existing plan and the grant of stock incentives to the Eligible Employees ofthe Company and its subsidiaries thereunder; which provided for approximately 1.15% of the equity shares of the Company then outstanding, amounting to approximately 5,00,00,000 equity shares. As on date of the Notice, 3,26,63,903 equity shares remain available for grant under the existing plan, representing the unutilized balance equity shares out of the original shareholder approved pool of 5,00,00,000 equity shares, and constituting approximately 0.8% of the outstanding equity shares of the Company as on the date of this Notice
As on the date of this Notice, the Company has 4,44,19,917 RSUs available for grant under all ESOP Plans, representing approximately 1.1% of the outstanding equity share capital of the Company This includes RSUs that have vested but remain unexercised, as well as RSUs that are yet to vest:
The shareholders had approved the Expanded Stock Ownership Program, 2019 ("2019 Plan" for a period of seven years, which is due to expire on June 21, 2026.
To ensure continuity of the Company's performance-based stock incentive plan and in line with its philosophy of aligning employee interests with long-term shareholder value creation, the Board has approved the amendments to ensure:
- Continuity of performance-based stock incentive program across an expanded employee base
- Sustained alignment of employee interests with long-term shareholder value creation
- Ability to attract; retain and incentivize talent in an increasingly competitive and evolving market key -
## The summary of the proposed amendments is as under:
## 1. Extension of the 2019 Plan tenure:
Extension of 2019 Plan for a further period of seven years from the date of shareholder approval The grants made under the 2019 Plan shall be made over seven (7) years, and the 2019 Plan shall be valid for a period of ten (10) years from the date ofreceipt of approval of shareholders:

- In line with the feedback received shareholders to align the Management compensation with long-term interests of shareholders, the introduction of a three-year rolling Relative Total Shareholder Return (TSR) as a vesting parameter for strengthening alignment with sustained shareholder value creation and reinforcing long-term market performance. from

news.headline: Q2FY27 Quarterly Result Announced for Infosys Ltd.
news.description: IT Consulting & Software company Infosys announced Q2FY27 results Standalone Financial Highlights:  Revenue from Operations: For Q2FY27, Standalone Revenue from Operations reached Rs 40,719 crore, representing a QoQ growth of 1.91% from Rs 39,957 crore in Q1FY27, and a YoY growth of 10.33% from Rs 36,907 crore in Q2FY26. For H1FY27, standalone revenue from operations stood at Rs 80,676 crore, displaying an increase of 11.77% YoY over Rs 72,182 crore in H1FY26. Total Income: Standalone Total Income was reported at Rs 42,421 crore in Q2FY27, indicating a QoQ expansion of 3.89% against Rs 40,831 crore in Q1FY27 and a YoY growth of 8.29% compared to Rs 39,175 crore in Q2FY26. For H1FY27, Standalone Total Income reached Rs 83,252 crore, which is a 10.51% YoY increase over Rs 75,333 crore in H1FY26. Profit Before Tax (PBT): For Q2FY27, Standalone PBT stood at Rs 10,905 crore, posting a sequential growth of 7.32% over Rs 10,161 crore in Q1FY27, and a YoY growth of 4.16% compared to Rs 10,469 crore in Q2FY26. For H1FY27, PBT increased by 10.13% YoY to Rs 21,067 crore against Rs 19,130 crore in H1FY26. Profit After Tax (PAT): Standalone PAT arrived at Rs 7,893 crore in Q2FY27, rising by 8.88% QoQ from Rs 7,249 crore in Q1FY27, and expanding by 1.73% YoY over Rs 7,759 crore in Q2FY26. For H1FY27, Standalone PAT grew 9.14% YoY to Rs 15,142 crore from Rs 13,874 crore in H1FY26. Earnings Per Share (EPS): Standalone Basic EPS stood at Rs 19.45 in Q2FY27, going up by 8.84% QoQ compared to Rs 17.87 in Q1FY27, and up by 4.12% YoY compared to Rs 18.68 in Q2FY26. For H1FY27, Basic EPS increased by 11.74% YoY to Rs 37.32 from Rs 33.40 in H1FY26.    Consolidated Financial Highlights:  Revenue from Operations: Consolidated Revenue from Operations was Rs 49,244 crore in Q2FY27, indicating a QoQ increase of 2.14% from Rs 48,211 crore in Q1FY27 and a YoY increase of 10.69% over Rs 44,490 crore in Q2FY26. For H1FY27, Consolidated Revenue from Operations expanded by 12.31% YoY to Rs 97,454 crore over Rs 86,769 crore in H1FY26. Total Income: Consolidated Total Income stood at Rs 50,092 crore in Q2FY27, indicating a QoQ uptick of 1.82% compared to Rs 49,195 crore in Q1FY27, and a YoY growth of 10.16% over Rs 45,472 crore in Q2FY26. For H1FY27, it reached Rs 99,286 crore, marking a YoY growth of 11.81% compared to Rs 88,793 crore in H1FY26. Profit Before Tax (PBT): For Q2FY27, Consolidated PBT came in at Rs 11,063 crore, rising sequentially by 0.32% over Rs 11,028 crore in Q1FY27, and up by 8.15% YoY over Rs 10,229 crore in Q2FY26. For H1FY27, Consolidated PBT arrived at Rs 22,091 crore, representing a 10.62% YoY growth from Rs 19,970 crore in H1FY26. Profit After Tax (PAT): Consolidated PAT reached Rs 7,838 crore in Q2FY27, expanding by 0.81% QoQ relative to Rs 7,775 crore in Q1FY27, and increasing by 6.28% YoY relative to Rs 7,375 crore in Q2FY26. For H1FY27, Consolidated PAT increased by 9.18% YoY to Rs 15,613 crore against Rs 14,300 crore in H1FY26. Earnings Per Share (EPS): Consolidated Basic EPS was Rs 19.32 in Q2FY27, ticking up by 0.68% QoQ from Rs 19.19 in Q1FY27, and showing a YoY growth of 8.78% from Rs 17.76 in Q2FY26. For H1FY27, Consolidated Basic EPS was reported at Rs 38.51, moving up by 11.72% YoY against Rs 34.47 in H1FY26.    Business & Segment Highlights:  Financial Services: This segment brought in the largest share of revenue at Rs 13,774 crore in Q2FY27 (compared to Rs 13,463 crore in Q1FY27 and Rs 12,320 crore in Q2FY26), with total half-yearly H1FY27 revenue at Rs 27,237 crore. Segment profit stood at Rs 3,644 crore for Q2FY27 and Rs 7,305 crore for H1FY27. Manufacturing: Segment revenue stood at Rs 7,913 crore in Q2FY27 (compared to Rs 7,668 crore in Q1FY27 and Rs 7,347 crore in Q2FY26), with total half-yearly H1FY27 revenue at Rs 15,581 crore. Segment profit was reported at Rs 1,694 crore for Q2FY27 and Rs 3,380 crore for H1FY27. Energy, Utilities, Resources and Services: This business generated a segment revenue of Rs 6,975 crore in Q2FY27 (compared to Rs 6,452 crore in Q1FY27 and Rs 5,945 crore in Q2FY26), with total half-yearly H1FY27 revenue at Rs 13,428 crore. Segment profit stood at Rs 1,986 crore for Q2FY27 and Rs 3,562 crore for H1FY27. Retail: Segment revenue was recorded at Rs 5,664 crore in Q2FY27 (compared to Rs 6,172 crore in Q1FY27 and Rs 5,639 crore in Q2FY26), with total half-yearly H1FY27 revenue at Rs 11,835 crore. Segment profit arrived at Rs 1,707 crore for Q2FY27 and Rs 3,408 crore for H1FY27. Communication: This segment registered a revenue of Rs 6,150 crore in Q2FY27 (compared to Rs 5,791 crore in Q1FY27 and Rs 5,397 crore in Q2FY26), with total half-yearly H1FY27 revenue at Rs 11,941 crore. Segment profit was Rs 1,146 crore for Q2FY27 and Rs 2,326 crore for H1FY27. Life Sciences: Segment revenue advanced significantly to Rs 4,145 crore in Q2FY27 (compared to Rs 3,842 crore in Q1FY27 and Rs 2,863 crore in Q2FY26), with total half-yearly H1FY27 revenue at Rs 7,986 crore. Segment profit came in at Rs 631 crore for Q2FY27 and Rs 1,250 crore for H1FY27. Hi-Tech: Revenue for this business stood at Rs 3,332 crore in Q2FY27 (compared to Rs 3,710 crore in Q1FY27 and Rs 3,703 crore in Q2FY26), with total half-yearly H1FY27 revenue at Rs 7,042 crore. Segment profit was Rs 795 crore for Q2FY27 and Rs 1,706 crore for H1FY27. All Other Segments: Reported a revenue of Rs 1,291 crore in Q2FY27 and Rs 2,404 crore in H1FY27, with segment profits standing at Rs 86 crore for Q2FY27 and Rs 162 crore for H1FY27. Large Deal Momentum: Large deal TCV reached USD 5.2 billion during Q2FY27, with net new wins accounting for 62% of the deal volume.  Salil Parekh, CEO & MD, said: “We had strong large deals of USD 5.2 billion, including a mega deal of over USD 2 billion, reinforcing our position as a trusted partner in the marketplace when clients embark on large and complex transformation programs. Our AI revenue was at 10.5% and grew 29% QoQ. As enterprises move to AI adoption at scale, the strong growth in AI revenues is a recognition of our differentiated market positioning and client confidence.” “We are advising some of the largest global enterprise on their AI strategy and continue to invest in deep domain and technology capabilities to bring new ideas and an integrated ecosystem to help businesses unlock AI value at scale.” Jayesh Sanghrajka, CFO, said: “We delivered operating margins of 21.0% in Q2 amidst heightened volatility. Focus on cost and operational efficiency measures while making the required investments, have led to stable margins.” “Free cash flow of $928 million, representing 113.3% of net profit, underscores the financial strength of the business. The Board has announced an interim dividend of Rs 26 per share, an increase of 13% from last year,” Result PDF

TO ALL STOCK EXCHANGES  BSE LIMITED  NATIONAL STOCK EXCHANGE OF INDIA LIMITED  NEW YORK STOCK EXCHANGE  October 23, 2026  Dear Sir/ Madam,  Sub: Outcome of the Board meeting  This has reference to our letter dated September 15, 2026, regarding the captioned subject. The Board, at their meeting held on October 22-23, 2026 transacted the following items of business:  Financial Results:  1.   Approved the audited consolidated financial results of the Company and its subsidiaries as per Indian Accounting Standards (“INDAS”) for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026;  2.   Approved the audited standalone financial results of the Company as per INDAS for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026;  3.   Approved the audited financial statements of the Company and its subsidiaries as per INDAS and  International Financial Reporting Standard (“IFRS”) for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026;  Dividend:  4.   Declared an interim dividend of ₹   26/- per equity share, fixed November 3, 2026 as a record date and November 11, 2026 as a payout date.  Stock grants:  5.   Based on the recommendations of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, the Board approved   the   grant   of   9,640   Restricted   Stock   Units   (‘RSUs’)   under   the   2015   Incentive Compensation Plan (’2015 Plan’) to eligible employees. The grants made under the 2015 Plan would vest equally over a period of three years. The RSUs will be granted w.e.f., November 1, 2026 and the exercise price will be equal to the par value of the share.

PRESS RELEASE  Infosys and Truist Strengthen Strategic Collaboration to Build a Global Capability Center in India  Bengaluru, India – October 19, 2026:   Infosys   (NSE, BSE, NYSE:INFY), a global leader in AI-first  business consulting and technology services, recently announced the expansion of its collaboration with  Truist , one of the largest US-based financial services companies, to support the bank’s continued build-out  of its AI-first Global Capability Center in Hyderabad. Together with Infosys, Truist is strengthening India’s role as a key global hub for innovation, talent, and digital capability.  Through this expanded collaboration, Infosys will utilize its deep financial services expertise and AI-first capabilities, to help accelerate scalable transformation and drive enterprise-wide value creation. As part of this effort, Truist is consolidating capabilities currently delivered through multiple supplier relationships in India into a more unified, integrated operating model. Infosys and Truist will celebrate the successful onboarding of more than 1,000 colleagues later this month, marking a significant milestone in the continued growth and expansion of the GCC.  The GCC represents Truist’s continued investment in building a scaled, future-ready innovation and operations hub designed to enhance client experiences, empower teammates, and help deliver a more digitally enabled and relationship-driven banking experience. Infosys will enable Truist to build, scale, and transition a self-sustaining center of excellence, integrating AI, technology, data, and operations into a single cohesive delivery framework. This model is designed to reduce third-party dependency, manage global delivery complexity, and cultivate deep, future-ready technology talent.  India represents a critical part of Truist’s evolving operating model, with a strong base of Truist contract professionals already contributing across engineering, data, and operations. ## Notice of the 45" Annual General Meeting
Notice is hereby given that the 45th Annual General Meeting (AGM) of the members of Infosys Limited ("the Company") will be held on Tuesday, June 23,2026,at 4.00 p.m. IST through video conference other audio-visual means ("VC") to transact the following business:
## Ordinary business
## Item no: 1 Adoption of financial statements
To consider and adopt the audited financial statements (including the consolidated financial statements) of the Company for the financial year ended March 31, 2026 and the reports of the Board of Directors ("the Board") and auditors thereon:
## Item no: 2 Declaration of dividend
To declare a final dividend of <25/- per equity share for the financial year ended March 31,2026.
## Item no. 3 Appointment of Nandan M: Nilekani as a director; liable to retire by rotation
To appoint a director in place of Nandan M. Nilekani (DIN: 00041245), who retires by rotation and being eligible, seeks reappointment:
Explanation: Based on the terms of appointment; executive directors, and the non-executive and non-independent chairman are subject to retirement by rotation: Nandan M Nilekani, who was initially appointed on August 24,2017 and last appointed on June 26,2024,and whose office is liable to retire at the ensuing AGM, being eligible; seeks reappointment: Based on his performance evaluation and the recommendation of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, the Board recommends his reappointment:
To consider and ifthought fit; to pass the following resolution as an ordinary resolution:
RESOLVED THAT pursuant to the provisions of Section 152 and other applicable provisions of the Companies Act; 2013,the approval of members of the Company, be and is hereby accorded to reappoint Nandan M. Nilekani (DIN: 00041245) as a director who is liable to retire by rotation.
## Special business
## Item no. 4 Approval of the proposed amendment to the Infosys Expanded Stock Ownership Program 2019 ("Amended 2019 Plan") and grant of stock incentives to the eligible employees of the Company under the Amended 2019 Plan
To consider and, if thought to pass the following resolution as a Special Resolution: fit,

## Explanatory Statement
## Background and context for item nos. 4 and 5
Approval of the proposed amendment to the Infosys Expanded Stock Ownership Program 2019 (such amended plan is hereinafter referred as the "Amended 2019 Plan") and grant of stock incentives to the eligible employees of the Company and its subsidiaries under the Amended 2019 Plan:
The Company has been a pioneer in India by rewarding its employees through stock ownership programs starting in 1994. This philosophy has created a culture of aligning employee and shareholder interests The 2015 Incentive Compensation Plan ("2015 Plan") was approved by shareholders pursuant to the postal ballot dated March 31,2016,and stock incentives continue to be granted to the eligible employees of the Company thereunder The vesting criteria for stock incentives under the 2015 Plan are largely time-based:
The existing plan was approved by shareholders pursuant to the Annual General Meeting held on June 22, 2019. The shareholders had approved the existing plan and the grant of stock incentives to the Eligible Employees ofthe Company and its subsidiaries thereunder; which provided for approximately 1.15% of the equity shares of the Company then outstanding, amounting to approximately 5,00,00,000 equity shares. As on date of the Notice, 3,26,63,903 equity shares remain available for grant under the existing plan, representing the unutilized balance equity shares out of the original shareholder approved pool of 5,00,00,000 equity shares, and constituting approximately 0.8% of the outstanding equity shares of the Company as on the date of this Notice
As on the date of this Notice, the Company has 4,44,19,917 RSUs available for grant under all ESOP Plans, representing approximately 1.1% of the outstanding equity share capital of the Company This includes RSUs that have vested but remain unexercised, as well as RSUs that are yet to vest:
The shareholders had approved the Expanded Stock Ownership Program, 2019 ("2019 Plan" for a period of seven years, which is due to expire on June 21, 2026.
To ensure continuity of the Company's performance-based stock incentive plan and in line with its philosophy of aligning employee interests with long-term shareholder value creation, the Board has approved the amendments to ensure:
- Continuity of performance-based stock incentive program across an expanded employee base
- Sustained alignment of employee interests with long-term shareholder value creation
- Ability to attract; retain and incentivize talent in an increasingly competitive and evolving market key -
## The summary of the proposed amendments is as under:
## 1. Extension of the 2019 Plan tenure:
Extension of 2019 Plan for a further period of seven years from the date of shareholder approval The grants made under the 2019 Plan shall be made over seven (7) years, and the 2019 Plan shall be valid for a period of ten (10) years from the date ofreceipt of approval of shareholders:
## 2. Strengthening alignment with Long-Term Shareholder Value creation and rationalization of Operational Metrics based on the inputs received from investors:
- In line with the feedback received shareholders to align the Management compensation with long-term interests of shareholders, the introduction of a three-year rolling Relative Total Shareholder Return (TSR) as a vesting parameter for strengthening alignment with sustained shareholder value creation and reinforcing long-term market performance. from
- Rationalization of the Operating metrics to ensure continued focus on the core financial metrics of revenue and margin, ensuring consistency and comparability over time: Given the rapid evolution of technology and business models, sub-segment metrics (like digital revenue growth) may become transient and less comparable

## Explanatory Statement
## Background and context for item nos. 4 and 5
Approval of the proposed amendment to the Infosys Expanded Stock Ownership Program 2019 (such amended plan is hereinafter referred as the "Amended 2019 Plan") and grant of stock incentives to the eligible employees of the Company and its subsidiaries under the Amended 2019 Plan:
The Company has been a pioneer in India by rewarding its employees through stock ownership programs starting in 1994. This philosophy has created a culture of aligning employee and shareholder interests The 2015 Incentive Compensation Plan ("2015 Plan") was approved by shareholders pursuant to the postal ballot dated March 31,2016,and stock incentives continue to be granted to the eligible employees of the Company thereunder The vesting criteria for stock incentives under the 2015 Plan are largely time-based:
The existing plan was approved by shareholders pursuant to the Annual General Meeting held on June 22, 2019. The shareholders had approved the existing plan and the grant of stock incentives to the Eligible Employees ofthe Company and its subsidiaries thereunder; which provided for approximately 1.15% of the equity shares of the Company then outstanding, amounting to approximately 5,00,00,000 equity shares. As on date of the Notice, 3,26,63,903 equity shares remain available for grant under the existing plan, representing the unutilized balance equity shares out of the original shareholder approved pool of 5,00,00,000 equity shares, and constituting approximately 0.8% of the outstanding equity shares of the Company as on the date of this Notice
As on the date of this Notice, the Company has 4,44,19,917 RSUs available for grant under all ESOP Plans, representing approximately 1.1% of the outstanding equity share capital of the Company This includes RSUs that have vested but remain unexercised, as well as RSUs that are yet to vest:
The shareholders had approved the Expanded Stock Ownership Program, 2019 ("2019 Plan" for a period of seven years, which is due to expire on June 21, 2026.
To ensure continuity of the Company's performance-based stock incentive plan and in line with its philosophy of aligning employee interests with long-term shareholder value creation, the Board has approved the amendments to ensure:
- Continuity of performance-based stock incentive program across an expanded employee base
- Sustained alignment of employee interests with long-term shareholder value creation
- Ability to attract; retain and incentivize talent in an increasingly competitive and evolving market key -
## The summary of the proposed amendments is as under:
## 1. Extension of the 2019 Plan tenure:
Extension of 2019 Plan for a further period of seven years from the date of shareholder approval The grants made under the 2019 Plan shall be made over seven (7) years, and the 2019 Plan shall be valid for a period of ten (10) years from the date ofreceipt of approval of shareholders:
## 2. Strengthening alignment with Long-Term Shareholder Value creation and rationalization of Operational Metrics based on the inputs received from investors:
- In line with the feedback received shareholders to align the Management compensation with long-term interests of shareholders, the introduction of a three-year rolling Relative Total Shareholder Return (TSR) as a vesting parameter for strengthening alignment with sustained shareholder value creation and reinforcing long-term market performance. from
- Rationalization of the Operating metrics to ensure continued focus on the core financial metrics of revenue and margin, ensuring consistency and comparability over time: Given the rapid evolution of technology and business models, sub-segment metrics (like digital revenue growth) may become transient and less comparable

## Client Wins & Testimonials
- Infosys collaborated with Mondelez International to drive its supply chain transformation through Al-enabled decision-making, data standardization, and intelligent enterprise workflows. Sanjay Gurbaxani, Global Vice President; Digital Supply Chain, Mondelez International, said, "From digitally connected supply chain to standardizing data and enabling more informed decision-making, the opportunity lies in bringing together people, processes, data, and technology to deliver meaningful business outcomes. As Al evolves towards agentic Al, the potential extends beyond generating insights to enable more autonomous, responsive, and intelligent workflows. The real value comes from embedding intelligence into everyday business decisions, rethinking established processes, and scaling solutions across the enterprise. With Infosys we are building a compelling solution where technology, aligned with business priorities, can become a catalyst for operational excellence and long-term impact '
- Infosys collaborated with Knorr-Bremse to accelerate its Al-enabled enterprise transformation. Satheeskaran Navaratnam, Chief Digital Officer & VP Transformation & Governance IT, Knorr-Bremse, said, At Knorr-Bremse, we are building a future-ready technology foundation that supports innovation and long-term value creation: Our Tech4Value program is central to this journey, helping us create a more agile, efficient; and scalable IT environment across the organization. By working with Infosys, we aim to make our technology estate as optimized and reliable as the systems we build for our customers, ensuring that every layer of our infrastructure is equipped to support the pace of change our business demands

October 23, 2026
Dear Sirl Madam,
## Sub: Qutcome of the Board meeting
This has reference to our letter dated September 15, 2026, regarding the captioned subject. The Board, at their meeting held on October 22-23, 2026 transacted the following items of business:
## Financial Results:
1. Approved the audited consolidated financial results of the Company and its subsidiaries as per Indian Accounting Standards ("INDAS") for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026;
2. Approved the audited standalone financial results of the Company as per INDAS for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026;
3. 3\_ Approved the audited financial statements of the Company and its subsidiaries as per INDAS and International Financial Reporting Standard ("IFRS") for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026;
## Dividend:
- 4\_ Declared an interim dividend of < 26/- per equity share, fixed November 3, 2026 as a record date
## Stock grants:
- 5\_ Based on the recommendations of the Nomination and Remuneration Committee, the Board approved the grant of 9,640 Restricted Stock Units (RSUs') under the 2015 Incentive Compensation Plan ('2015 Plan') to eligible employees. The grants made under the 2015 Plan would vest equally over a period of three years. The RSUs will be granted W.e.f,, November 1, 2026 and the exercise will be equal to the par value of the share. price
## Allotment of equity shares:
- 6\_ Allotted 15,578 equity shares of face value of < 5/- each, pursuant to exercise of Restricted Stock Units by eligible employees as hereunder:
- 2,841 equity shares under the 2015 Incentive Compensation Plan;
- 12,737 equity shares under the Infosys Expanded Stock Ownership Program 2019.
Consequently, effective from October 23, 2026, the issued and subscribed share capital of the Company stands increased to < 20,29,14,60,780/- divided into 4,05,82,92,156 equity shares of <5/each:
The Board meeting was held on October 22 and 23, 2026. The Board meeting on October 23, 2026 commenced at 12.27 PM IST and concluded at 4.00 PM IST.
We are hereby enclosing herewith the financial results, press releases, and other annexures mentioned above. The same will also be made available on the Company's website WWW infosys com:
